Title: Combat sequence: must acting vampire act first?

Messages.Author: James C. Clover
Messages.Body:
I had always taken for granted that if your vampire performs an action
and is blocked that you start maneuvering, you declare strike first, etc.
However, I happened to be browsing the rulebook and came across this
startling paragraph:

"In general, the player of the acting minion must decide each phase if
the minion will use a card or do something before the blocking minion.
If the acting minion foregoes this opportunity to act first, it cannot
reconsider and take action, except in direct response to the blocking
minion."

Whoah! What's up? Does this mean if I am playing a combat deck, and my
prey is playing a Presence vote deck, that I can wait to see if he plays
Majesty before I waste my nasty damage card?

There have been many times when I found myself playing Gangrel against my
friend's Toreador with Majesty. I bleed, he blocks, he waits for me to
whip out my Wolf Claws so he can play his Majesty, thereby making me
waste a precious aggravated damage card.

This brings up another question. Can I play Wolf Claws (since it isn't a
strike card) right between Choose Strike and Resolve Strike (thereby
eliminating the possibility of wasting it on a dodge or Majesty)?

But getting back to my original question, could somebody please clarify
what I can or cannot do as the acting vampire? Thanks.
--
Simeon

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
In article <jcloverD...@netcom.com>,

James C. Clover <jcl...@netcom.com> wrote:
>"In general, the player of the acting minion must decide each phase if
>the minion will use a card or do something before the blocking minion.
>If the acting minion foregoes this opportunity to act first, it cannot
>reconsider and take action, except in direct response to the blocking
>minion."
>
>Whoah! What's up? Does this mean if I am playing a combat deck, and my
>prey is playing a Presence vote deck, that I can wait to see if he plays
>Majesty before I waste my nasty damage card?

If you are blocking your Prey's acting minion, yes.

>There have been many times when I found myself playing Gangrel against my
>friend's Toreador with Majesty. I bleed, he blocks, he waits for me to
>whip out my Wolf Claws so he can play his Majesty, thereby making me
>waste a precious aggravated damage card.
>
>This brings up another question. Can I play Wolf Claws (since it isn't a
>strike card) right between Choose Strike and Resolve Strike (thereby
>eliminating the possibility of wasting it on a dodge or Majesty)?

Yes, you may play Wolf Claws after both strikes have been declared and before
they start resolving, allowing you to save your aggravated damage until
you *know* it won't be dodged or S:CE'ed.

>But getting back to my original question, could somebody please clarify
>what I can or cannot do as the acting vampire? Thanks.

Acting vampire: declines to play further stealth to complete the action
-- he is blocked.
Acting Vampire: chooses whether or not to play a card (Freak Drive, e.g.)
before combat starts.
(Then blocking minion does the same)
Acting vampire: chooses whether or not to play any combat cards before range
is choosen (Torn Sign Post, etc.)
(Then blocking Minion does the same).
Acting vampire: chooses whether or not to play a maneuver first.
(Then blocking Minion does the same or responds- start looping).
Acting vampire: chooses his initial strike
(Then blocking Minion does the same (except in Jyhad if the acting vamp's
strike was to end combat: this resolves prematurely. this has been fixed
in V:tES)).
All strikes done at first strike resolve.
All non-first strike strikes resolve.
Acting Minion chooses whether ot not to gain additional strikes.
(Then blocking Minion does the same).
Acting Minion chooses whether or not to initiate the Press sequence.
(Then blocking Minion does the same or responds- start looping).

determine range. (or tap elysium and combat ends 9) )

ok, now you choose strikes. you pick hands and he says "me too"

you say "wolfs claws" and he says ouch.

Messages.Author: Ken Mikolaj
Messages.Body:
The proper way to use a card like Wolf Claws is to wait until your
opponent declares his strike. After the strike is declared, use your
Wolf Claws...it is then too late to Dodge, Majesty...etc.

Hi Mark,
Hi James,
Actually the magic word is STRIKE:, when a card text includes the
word Strike followed by a colon, then that card represents your actual
strike. So in James example, Chester is the acting vampire and must
declare his intentions first. Chester doesn't manuver, so he can not
change his mind and manuver later unless Kalista manuvers.... However
players must always declare a strike, so once range is determined Chester
must declare his strike first, and since Undead Strength is a strike,
Chester must declare it before he knows if Kallista is dodging. Wolf
claws and Claws of the Dead do not say Strike:, therefore you may play
them after you see if the target is dodging....

answered. Let me clarify. Please read the text above, which I quoted
from the small rules book. It would seem to suggest that the following
could take place:

(I control Chester DuBois; my prey controls Kallista)

Chester bleeds.
Kallista blocks.
Me: "No maneuver."
Prey: "No maneuver."
Me: "Hmm.. I'd hate to waste Undead Strength if she's going to dodge...
Uh... you go first."
Prey: "Hand strike."
Me: "Undead Strength superior!"
...

See what I'm saying? This looks ridiculous, but according to the text of
the rule book, I can forgoe the opportunity to act first, yet I can act
in response to the blocker's play.
